narrative:
The model predicts you have a 15% chance of failing your final year. While this is not a high probability, it is enough for the school to require you to take remedial courses as a precaution.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this prediction were your number of past class failures, your desire to pursue higher education, and your weekend alcohol consumption. Surprisingly, the strongest influence came from your clean record of zero past failures. Among students who passed, this is exactly the average, so the model saw this as a reassuring sign that actually worked against the failure prediction. Your strong ambition to continue into higher education also pushed the outcome toward passing, as every student who passed shared this same goal.

However, your weekend alcohol consumption worked in the opposite direction. Even though you drink very little on weekends compared with many peers, this habit still nudged the model slightly toward expecting difficulties. These three elements together created a borderline prediction that tipped just enough to flag a risk of failure.

To improve, focus on protecting your strong motivation and zero-failure record by addressing the one area the model highlighted: consider how even moderate weekend socialising might be quietly affecting your consistency. Cutting back further or planning your time more deliberately around weekends could give you the extra margin needed to turn that 15% risk into a confident pass.
